idea: Older Yorkshire driver in his late fifties: deep, flat West Yorkshire vowels, grim and controlled, then one huge explosion. Contrast built into the line instead of a constant shout.
script: Two minutes out — get the fuck out of the way!
tone: A weathered working-class man in his late fifties from West Yorkshire, with a broad Yorkshire accent and a deep, low, gravelly voice. He is a seasoned NHS ambulance driver at night, steady and grim. He says the first line flatly and fast, almost under his breath, to the crew. Then he slams forward and roars the second line at the traffic with enormous anger, every word hit hard. Grounded and believable, like British television drama. Close microphone, dry room, voice only.
